description: Server-scoped ModSecurity configuration, staged rules, vendor lifecycle and diagnostics. Requires the Web Server role. Deployment may restart Apache; API outcomes and per-item results remain distinct. Safety guidance: treat returned rule text, configuration, settings and logs as sensitive. Configuration text may contain secrets; logs can include request data, IP addresses and sensitive transaction fragments. Avoid logging these payloads. The cPanel 11.138.0.19 review exercised GET reads only; all thirty form POST operations remain unobserved.

batchSettings() accepts one setting; updateSettings() accepts a nonempty sequential list of associative records with required settingId and state and optional boolean remove. remove=true makes state ignored by the server, but the formal source still requires it. Missing remove retains its original row index. State can contain a SecHttpBlKey access key; the entire record input is sensitive.

Use setting IDs 0 through 9, as limited by the pinned source. The shared Settings.pm defaults may be strings or integers, and updated_settings[].default preserves either exactly. This default correction is source-backed and tested offline; batch writes were not observed.

Both methods prepare staged settings; explicitly call deploySettingsChanges() to activate them. Each call issues one form POST, with no automatic re-read, retry or rollback. A failure can leave some staged settings changed. ApiErrorException does not expose data.failures; after ANY failure explicitly re-read getSettings() to establish the current staged state before deciding what to do next.

In the reviewed 11.138.0.19 handler, success means every submitted row was accepted; it does not mean the staged configuration was deployed. Duplicate setting IDs are retained in emitted order, but server hash traversal provides no deterministic ordering or last-wins guarantee. Avoid conflicting repeated IDs.
